package.name: NanoId
package.description: Short, URL-safe, unpredictable identifiers in the Nano ID format

modules.name: Alphabet
modules.header:
What an identifier is drawn from, and the ways a caller-supplied alphabet can be unusable.
The default alphabet is Nano ID's own: the sixty-four characters that are safe unescaped in a URL, a file name and
most identifiers, in the order the reference implementation lists them. Sixty-four is a power of two, so each
random byte yields one character with no rejection and no bias. The order is kept so that the same random bytes
produce the same identifier here as in every other implementation, which is what makes the test vectors shared.
A custom alphabet must be between two and 256 distinct ASCII characters. One character carries no information,
more than 256 cannot be indexed by a byte, a repeated character makes that character more likely than the others,
and a character outside ASCII is several bytes in UTF-8 where an identifier is promised to be one byte per
character.

modules.name: Generate
modules.header:
Filling a caller's buffer with an identifier, from the system's generator or from a supplied source.
Each character is a random byte masked down to the smallest power of two that covers the alphabet. A masked value
past the end of the alphabet is thrown away rather than folded back in with a remainder, because folding would
make the first characters of the alphabet more likely than the rest. With the default alphabet the mask is the
whole alphabet and nothing is thrown away; with a custom one at most half the bytes are, and bytes are requested
in batches sized so that one batch usually suffices.
The batch of random bytes is zeroized before returning, since an identifier is often a secret such as a session
token and the bytes it was drawn from say what it is. A failure leaves the destination zeroized too, rather than
holding the first part of an identifier that a careless caller might use anyway.

modules.name: NanoId
modules.header:
A standard identifier as a value: twenty-one characters of the default alphabet, held inline.
Most programs want exactly one kind of identifier, and a value is easier to pass, store and compare than a buffer
and a length. The text is stored as it is written, so `Text` borrows it without any conversion and two equal
identifiers have equal bytes.
Parsing is strict about the form: exactly twenty-one characters, each from the default alphabet. An identifier
from a custom alphabet or of another length is a different kind of value and stays in a buffer.

doc.summary: Nano ID's default alphabet: the sixty-four URL-safe characters `A`–`Z`, `a`–`z`, `0`–`9`, `_` and `-`.
doc.markdown:
Nano ID's default alphabet: the sixty-four URL-safe characters `A`–`Z`, `a`–`z`, `0`–`9`, `_` and `-`.
Listed in the reference implementation's order, so the same random bytes give the same identifier here as there.

doc.summary: The default identifier length, in characters: twenty-one.
doc.markdown:
The default identifier length, in characters: twenty-one.
Twenty-one characters of the default alphabet carry 126 random bits, more than the 122 of a version 4 UUID, in
twenty-one characters where the UUID takes thirty-six.

doc.summary: Why an identifier could not be generated.
doc.markdown:
Why an identifier could not be generated.
Failure-only: a filled destination is the success channel of `! NanoIdError`. Copy, owning nothing. The alphabet
cases are found before any random bytes are requested, so they never consume entropy.

cases.name: AlphabetTooSmall
cases.doc: The alphabet has fewer than two characters, so an identifier from it carries no information.

cases.name: AlphabetTooLarge
cases.doc: The alphabet has more than 256 characters, more than one random byte can choose between.

cases.name: DuplicateCharacter
cases.doc:
A character appears twice, which would make it twice as likely as the rest. The offset is the second
occurrence.

cases.name: NonAsciiCharacter
cases.doc:
A byte outside ASCII. The offset is that byte. Each character of an identifier is one byte, which a character
that takes several bytes in UTF-8 cannot be.

cases.name: Entropy
cases.doc: The operating system could not supply random bytes, for the reason carried.

doc.summary: Checks that `alphabet` can be drawn from without bias.
doc.markdown:
Checks that `alphabet` can be drawn from without bias.
It must hold between two and 256 characters, all ASCII and all distinct. Reports `AlphabetTooSmall`,
`AlphabetTooLarge`, `NonAsciiCharacter` or `DuplicateCharacter`, the last two with the offset of the offending
byte. Runs in time linear in the alphabet's length and allocates nothing.

params.name: alphabet
params.markdown: the characters an identifier would be drawn from

doc.returns: success when the alphabet is usable

items.name: GenerateNanoId
items.signature: pub func GenerateNanoId(into: var char8[..]) -> ! EntropyError

doc.summary: Fills the whole of `into` with an identifier from the default alphabet, using the operating system's generator.
doc.markdown:
Fills the whole of `into` with an identifier from the default alphabet, using the operating system's generator.
The identifier is as long as `into`; `NanoIdLength` characters is the standard length. Each character is one
random byte, so a twenty-one-character identifier costs twenty-one bytes of entropy. Reports what the system
reported when it could not supply random bytes, leaving `into` zeroized. An empty `into` succeeds and requests
nothing.
doc.returns: success when every character was written

items.name: GenerateNanoId
items.signature: pub func GenerateNanoId(into: var char8[..], alphabet: char8[..]) -> ! NanoIdError

doc.summary: Fills the whole of `into` with an identifier drawn from `alphabet`, using the operating system's generator.
doc.markdown:
Fills the whole of `into` with an identifier drawn from `alphabet`, using the operating system's generator.
Every character of `alphabet` is equally likely at every position. Reports an alphabet failure from
`ValidateAlphabet` before requesting any random bytes, leaving `into` untouched, and `Entropy` when the system
could not supply them, leaving `into` zeroized.

params.name: alphabet
params.markdown: between two and 256 distinct ASCII characters

doc.returns: success when every character was written

items.name: GenerateNanoIdFrom
items.signature: pub func GenerateNanoIdFrom(source: &var EntropySource, into: var char8[..], alphabet: char8[..]) -> ! NanoIdError

doc.summary: Fills the whole of `into` with an identifier drawn from `alphabet`, using random bytes from `source`.
doc.markdown:
Fills the whole of `into` with an identifier drawn from `alphabet`, using random bytes from `source`.
The seam for a test, or for a caller with its own generator: the identifier is exactly as unpredictable as the
bytes `source` supplies, so a deterministic source gives deterministic identifiers. Reports an alphabet failure
from `ValidateAlphabet` before using `source`, leaving `into` untouched, and `Entropy` with what `source`
reported, leaving `into` zeroized.

params.name: source
params.markdown: where the random bytes come from

params.name: alphabet
params.markdown: between two and 256 distinct ASCII characters

doc.returns: success when every character was written

doc.markdown:
A Nano ID of the standard form: twenty-one characters from `NanoIdAlphabet`.
Copy, holding its text inline and owning nothing. Equality and ordering compare the text byte by byte.

doc.summary: A new identifier from the operating system's generator.
doc.markdown:
A new identifier from the operating system's generator.
Costs twenty-one bytes of entropy and allocates nothing. Reports what the system reported when it could not
supply random bytes, and produces no identifier in that case.
doc.returns: the identifier, or why none could be made

members.name: Parse
members.signature: pub func Parse(text: char8[..]) -> NanoId ! NanoIdParseError

doc.summary: Reads a standard identifier from its text.
doc.markdown:
Reads a standard identifier from its text.
Reports `WrongLength` unless the text is exactly twenty-one bytes, and `InvalidCharacter` at the first byte
outside the default alphabet. A refused parse produces no value. Runs in constant time for a text of the
right length and allocates nothing.
doc.returns: the identifier, or why the text is not one

doc.markdown:
The identifier's twenty-one characters.
Borrows the value: the slice reads the value's own storage and must not outlive it. Cannot fail and
allocates nothing.
doc.returns: the text, always `NanoIdLength` bytes of the default alphabet

doc.summary: Whether two identifiers are the same.
doc.markdown:
Whether two identifiers are the same.
Compares every byte whatever it finds, so the time taken does not reveal how much of a guessed identifier was
right. Cannot fail and allocates nothing.
doc.returns: whether the two have the same text

doc.summary: The order of two identifiers' texts, byte by byte.
doc.markdown:
The order of two identifiers' texts, byte by byte.
Identifiers are random, so this order means nothing beyond being total and stable, which is what a sorted
container needs. Cannot fail and allocates nothing.

cases.name: WrongLength
cases.doc:
The text is not twenty-one bytes long. The offset is the text's length when it is too short, and the first
byte past the form when it is too long.

cases.name: InvalidCharacter
cases.doc: A character that is not in the default alphabet. The offset is that character.

doc.markdown:
